reason: Not refuted. The core claim holds analytically, not only in the scanner's 12-world MC. With (a)=X+eps+max(i,0), (b)=X+eps+i+max(d,0) and (c)=X+eps+max(i+d,0): whenever i+d>=0, (b)-(c)=max(0,-d). So once sd(d) is large relative to i, (b) beats (c) on E[max], and (c)'s cliff (~P(eps<=0)*P(i+d<0)) is above (a)'s (~P(eps<=0)*P(i<0)). I ran an independent MC over 96 worlds (scratchpad pairsim.py: i mean 1e-3/2e-3, P(i<0) 0.1/0.2, six d regimes with sd 0.3-3e-3, rho 0/0.5, eps as a coin flip or exactly 0 in 70% of draws with a tie counted as the cliff). Results: (c) is dominated on both metrics in 61/96; its cliff is above (a) in 90/96; it has the top E[max] in only 18/96, and those are mainly low-variance worlds (sd(d)<=0.5e-3) or the P(i<0)=0.2, rho=0.5 corner, which matches the finding's 'middle option' caveat. The premise of the round-12 judge (knob delta ~+0.0008 lab; round12/report.notes.md l.7) does not hold for the DC knob after D1 (dc0.30 = -0.005 public vs lab +0.0013/0). So this is a legitimate recheck of I-298 restricted to class C, not a closed line in disguise; A/B stay unchanged. The finding also understates point (1). Lowrefine only moves 12 nodes in 121,252, none near GT, and the node count is unchanged (FACTS F-MOD-17). So eps on private may be EXACTLY 0, and a tie at X loses to the ~350 earlier x138 copies. That makes #38's hedge even weaker and helps (b) further. Feasibility: this is advice on the finals pair only. No code, no submit, runtime 0, not a new mechanism (R8 not binding). The gate is honest: a user letter logged before the first poll.log header with 56598763/56598765 terminal (~12:30Z), asked in the 07:30Z brief; the default stays (a). Limits: the world counts are illustration only (I-092 false precision), and sd(d) on private is inferred from one public embryo. The value is small and conditional.
fix: Adopt as written with these edits. (1) Label every world count ('8/12', '10/12') as ILLUSTRATIVE (cf. I-092), never as a rule input. Base the brief on the analytic statement: for a high-variance knob, (c) = {V*_C, #38} is worse than (b) on E[max] and worse than (a) on cliff. (2) Curator note for I-297/I-298: 'high-variance knob (DC, D1 04:58Z) -> the {V*, #38} shape is dominated. #38 hedges only if eps > 0. eps may be exactly 0 on private (lowrefine moves 12 nodes, none near GT, node count unchanged; F-MOD-17), and a tie at X loses to earlier copies.' Do not turn the eps=0 point into a new rule for the base pair (a); it stays the default. (3) Scope guard: apply only to class-C DC refs 43/44. If both display 0.954 or lower, no V*_C exists and nothing changes. A/B (lp30, fm45) keep L9 {V*, #38}. (4) Brief wording: (a) default / (b) upside (higher expected private, similar or somewhat higher cliff) / (c) not recommended. Log the letter with date -u before the first poll.log header showing 43/44 terminal; a later letter is labelled post-hoc. No new submit, build or rung.
realistic_gain: Only conditional. It applies if 43 or 44 displays >=0.955 (prior ~0.3 combined) AND the user allows class C (~0.3-0.5). Then (b) instead of (c): about +0.1..+0.5e-3 E[max] private and about -0.01..-0.15 cliff probability (my MC, sd(d)>=1e-3). Unconditional: ~1-7e-5 expected private, runtime 0. The main value is avoiding a bad default shape (the L9 shape carried over to class C by reflex).
